w: At 10.35 am Swamishri arrived at an assembly of tribal devotees on the mandir grounds. The stage backdrop of a tribal hut, earthen grain storage containers, a meshwork of palm leaves and a parrot cage created a perfect tribal domestic ambience. After a few speeches on tribal upliftment and a colorful tribal folk dance Swamishri appreciated the 7,000 tribals who had come for the one day convention and emphasized that they should not fall prey to addictions and material enticements and remain steadfast in following the ideals of Hindu dharma.
Swamishri visited Dangra for darshan of the Hari Mandir built as a memorial shrine (samadhi sthan) to Jaga Swami and blessed the local devotees.

Swamishri arrived in Rajkot at 12.35 p.m. In the evening assembly, the kishores performed a welcome dance and the volunteers of Rajkot mandal presented a debate on the supremacy of Shriji Maharaj. Finally Swamishri addressed the assembly of devotees.

Today marked the 92nd patotsav of Sarangpur mandir. The patotsav rituals of the murtis of pujan and abhishek in all five shrines began after mangala arti. After these Vedic rituals, an annakut was offered in each shrine. Swamishri then performed the patotsav arti. After puja, Swamishri blessed the assembly, “The patotsav has been well celebrated today with arti, pujan, bhajan and kirtan. Every year the patotsav is held with all rituals. Some people say that it is because God’s powers have decreased. But God’s powers do not decrease; ours do. That is why we have to perform pujan. God is divine and his divinity never decreases. But this is done so that our bhakti and affection for God increases, we experience peace in life and our satsang increases.” Then Swamishri read Vachanamrut Sarangpur-7 and explained, “Our mind is constantly wandering; it never remains still. Just like a monkey is always roaming, so is the mind. It flirts from one thought to another. It travels abroad – without a plane, ticket or passport – and returns. But where the thoughts of the mind become calm is known as Naimisharanya Kshetra. Where our senses, worldly thoughts and desires are destroyed is known as Naimisharanya Kshetra. “Where is Naimisharanya Kshetra? It is wherever the ekantik Sadhu of God is…. By associating with such a Satpurush, no attachment to worldly objects remains.”

In the evening satsang assembly Viveksagar Swami delivered a discourse. Thereafter, a drama on ideal devotees ‘Satsangi to tene kahiye’, written by Adarshjivan Swami, was performed by youths. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly, “With satsang and bhakti, one should not become egoistic, jealous or harbor ill-will towards others. When one does not have the predominance of satsang in life, one is faced with problems at every step. The devotion one offers to God becomes useful, just as Dada Khachar, Parvatbhai and others had done.”

6 May 2009, Mumbai A youth who had an addiction came to Swamishri. He ate ghutka (shredded tobacco with flavour). Swamishri questioned, “Do you feel that your addiction is wrong?” “Yes.” “Then give it up. How long does it take to quit for someone who thinks it is wrong!” “I’ll give it up slowly,” the youth replied mildly. “Will you take poison if I give it to you?” Swamishri asked explicitly. “No.” “Tobacco is poison. You shouldn’t give it up slowly. If someone were to tell you to go to America after all the arrangements were made, would you go slowly? Similarly, you should quit in one go. Pray to God and you’ll be able to give it up.” Swamishri blessed the youth.
For the sake of one’s child

15 May 2009, Mumbai A father and son came for Swamishri’s darshan and blessings. The son was of a tender age. His father was habituated to drinking alcohol. Swamishri asked him, “How would you feel if your son started drinking?” The father remained silent. Swamishri asked the child, “What does your father drink?” Before the boy could answer his father averred, “He doesn’t know as yet?” Swamishri picked up his words and advised, “When he comes to know and starts drinking, how will you react?” Give it up for the sake of your child. There is no need to drink liquor at all. Everything other than eating, praying to God and looking after one’s responsibilities is wasteful.”Swamishri’s words produced a desirable effect.

After the darshan of Thakorji, when Pramukh Swami Maharaj came down in the lift, a youth's drum set had been placed there to be sanctified. After placing flowers on the drum set, Swamishri took the drumsticks lying on the drum set in his hand and, striking four or five different drums in the style of Sivamani, created a divine sound. Finally he also struck the big gong with the stick and made it ring. He gave everyone a memory.

At yesterday's Sunday assembly, twenty thousand devotees were present. All these devotees were served fresh mango juice. And the very best kinds of mangoes had been used. Pramukh Swami Maharaj was pleased to hear this.

After the talk was over, Swamishri said, "This Siddheshwar Swami has come from Surendranagar and is going back to Surendranagar, so pack the very best mangoes for Thakorji of Surendranagar. Pack Kesar, Hafus, all of them, so that Thakorji eats and the sadhus eat too."

After the darshan of Thakorji, when Pramukh Swami Maharaj came down in the lift, a youth's drum set had been placed there to be sanctified. After placing flowers on the drum set, Swamishri took in his hand the drumstick lying on the drum set itself, and striking four or five different drums in the style of Sivamani, brought forth a divine sound. Finally he also struck the big gong with the stick and made it ring. He gave everyone something to remember.

At yesterday's Sunday assembly twenty thousand devotees were present. All these devotees were served fresh mango juice. Moreover, the very best kind of mangoes had been used. Hearing this, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was pleased.

When the talk was over, Swamishri said, "This Siddheshwar Swami has come from Surendranagar and is going back to Surendranagar, so pack the very best mangoes for him for Thakorji in Surendranagar. Pack Kesar, Hafus and all these, so that Thakorji eats them and the sants eat them too."
When Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the balcony to give darshan to the sadhus and devotees, seeing the devotees, he exclaimed, "I very much wish to meet everyone."

To convey this feeling of Swamishri to all the devotees sitting below, a microphone was immediately brought and held before Swamishri. Swamishri said, "I feel like doing dandvat to everyone; I very much wish to meet you, but..." As he spoke, Swamishri was overcome with emotion. He could not say any more.
Where else but in our guru parampara can one see such a close relationship between guru and disciples?
